full_judgment:
6. Both the suits were heard analogously and the trial Court dismissed the suit for specific performance of contract and decreed the suit for eviction. The present petitioners preferred First Appeal No. 152 of 2016 and First Appeal No. 93 of 2016 respectively in the High Court Division and the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and decree, dismissed both the appeals. Thus, the petitioners have filed these two civil petitions for leave to appeal. 

 7. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the petitions, submits that though the plaintiffs have been able to prove the story of talk of sale, execution of bainanama, payment of consideration and the fact of refusal to execute and register the sale deed, the Courts below most illegally dismissed the suit for specific performance of contract and decreed the suit for eviction. 

 8. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali and Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents in both the petitions, in their submissions supported the judgments and decrees of the Courts below. 

 10. The relief of specific performance's discretionary, and it is not to be given merely because it is lawful to do. So, but it is governed by sound judicial principles. The exercise of discretion to order specific performance would require the court to be satisfied that the circumstances are such that it is equitable to make such a decree. 

 15. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we do not find any illegality and irregularity in the judgment and decree of the Courts below.
